text:
Elaine: heads-up — during the load test at ~17:20 UTC the us-west GPU thin-pool hit soft-limit and we saw automated fallback to eu-central. cost spike and increased p99.
Jon: saw this — traffic shifted automatically, but KV cache misses spiked which hurt latency. logs attached to the incident ticket.
Ajay: do we know which thin-pool metric triggered the fallback? was it 'available_gpus' or the thinpool daemon check?
SRE-Bot: fallback initiated by routing-policy v2.3 when 'thin_pool_utilization' > 92% for 30s.
Elaine: confirmed — threshold was 92%. the autoscaler didn't provision faster because the thin-pool prewarm job is rate-limited.
Marco: that prewarm rate-limit is the old safety guard. we under-provisioned for synthetic spike scenarios.
Jon: immediate mitigation during the test: manually increased thin-pool target from 20 -> 40 and bumped autoscale window to 60s. reduced further failovers.
Ajay: notes for runbook: we need an explicit step to check 'thin_pool_prewarmer' tokens and to escalate to Infra on-call if prewarm is saturated.
Elaine: agreed. also add a step to capture KV cache snapshot before shifting traffic. we lost warmup state when requests moved regions.
Marco: action: add a prewarming healthcheck metric 'prewarmer_queue_length' and alert at > 50 for 2 minutes.
SRE-Bot: suggested runbook edit: add commands for on-call to run prewarm-boost: 
```
# temporarily increase prewarm tokens
curl -XPOST https://infra-api.redwood.local/prewarm -d '{"tokens":50}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN'
```
Ajay: also recommend lowering fallback aggressiveness: change routing-policy v2.3 fallback window from 30s -> 90s when autoscaler is scaling. otherwise we keep bouncing.
Jon: cost note: fallback to eu-central added ~27% token-cost increase in that 45m window. include cost impact in postmortem.
Elaine: post-incident updates I want in runbook:
- prewarm healthcheck + alert
- clear escalation path to infra-team + phone number
- standard commands to boost prewarmer (see SRE-Bot snippet)
- instructions to snapshot and ship KV cache to target region
- guidance to temporarily prioritize local region routing if p95 latency < 600ms
Marco: technical detail for KV snapshot step: we should use the kv-sync job: 
```
kv-sync --src us-west --dst eu-central --keys-prefix=/cache/prefix --mode=incremental
```
Ajay: add an automated task: after fallback event, run a background 'cache-seed' where a subset of traffic is mirrored (5%) to warm caches in fallback region before full cutover.
Jon: ops runbook bot: can we add a checklist item to verify autoscaler min-gpus per nodepool is not zero? we had a nodepool with min=0 that delayed capacity.
Ops-Runbook-Bot: checklist item added draft: 'verify nodepool.min_gpus > 1 for thin-pool critical pools'.
Elaine: person assignments:
- Marco -> implement prewarmer metrics + alert (ETA 48h)
- Ajay -> update routing-policy config & add cache-seed logic (ETA 72h)
- Jon -> run cost analysis and update incident ticket with numbers (ETA 24h)
- Elaine -> update runbook text and rollout doc (ETA 48h)
SRE-Bot: automated suggestion: add a canary test that simulates 2x synthetic load every deploy to thin-pool controllers.
Marco: I'll add a canary job in cicd for thinpool-controller.
Ajay: follow-up: we should also add SLA note for customers who prefer strict regional routing; currently fallback can cross billing regions. need product + sales sign-off.
Elaine: yes — ops + product to sync. product to decide whether to expose 'no-cross-region-fallback' flag.
Jon: final: add one-liner to playbook about cost awareness when shifting regions: 'Expect cost uplift; inform billing and flag to finance if > 20% increase in a 1h window.'
Elaine: thanks all. I'll push the runbook edits now and request review. :thumbsup:
Ajay: thanks — will follow up with PRs.
Marco: thanks — will prioritize metrics work.
SRE-Bot: incident thread closed, follow-ups tracked in ticket #INC-2026-455.
